_comment: What `gc dynamics` runs for this paper, and what the trajectory has to show before it
ships. BUILD_SPEC Stage 4: if a trajectory does not support what the paper claims, do
not ship that trajectory, and say so in ISSUES.md.
This is the hardest system in the set. 8E1X is 2.68 A, has 77 unobserved residues
including a 29-residue N-terminal tail, and carries TWO PHOSPHOTYROSINES in the
activation loop. Amber14 has no phosphotyrosine parameters, so they are reverted to
tyrosine and that is recorded: the claims tested here are hinge and gatekeeper contacts
at the other end of the kinase, which the activation loop's phosphorylation state does
not make or break. A run that needed the phosphorylated form would need parameters this
pipeline does not have, and would not ship.
Compound 30 carries a d3-methyl amide. OpenFF has no deuterium and the mass does not
change the pose, so it is simulated as hydrogen and reported as such.
decided: 2026-09-14: 5 ns production per structure, a contact counts as supported at 50 per cent occupancy, an absence at 20 per cent, ligand drift under 2 A median. Phosphotyrosines reverted to tyrosine, recorded here and in ISSUES.md.

structures.protonation_note: Neutral. The aminopyrazolo-pyrimidine and the amide are not protonated at pH 7.4, and the tetrahydrofuran is an ether.
structures.gaps_note: 8E1X chain A has a 5-residue internal gap, which is modelled, and a 29-residue N-terminal and 6-residue C-terminal gap, which are not: an unresolved tail is disordered, and inventing one adds a flapping arm that dominates the RMSF of everything near it.
structures.nonstandard_note: PTR 466 and PTR 586 are phosphotyrosines. Amber14 carries no parameters for them, so PDBFixer reverts both to tyrosine. The claims tested here are at the hinge and the gatekeeper, not the activation loop.
